question: What percentage of tests will be positive for seasonal human coronaviruses (all types) in the United States for the week ending October 24, 2026, in CDC data?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the percent of tests positive for seasonal human coronaviruses (all types) in the United States for the week ending 2026-10-24 in CDC's the National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS) percent positivity data (data.cdc.gov dataset rgnm-fkqb), as posted on 2026-10-30.
research:
I pulled the weekly national numbers straight from the resolution dataset through the SODA API. One caveat: the copy I could read was refreshed after the cutoff. I used only weeks that would have been published by 2026-10-05, ending with the week of 2026-09-26. Those values may have been revised slightly since they first appeared. I left out the week ending 10-03 and the target week.

## 1. Resolution source
- The dataset is data.cdc.gov rgnm-fkqb (NREVSS percent positivity), filtered to level = National, pathogen = HCOV, subtype = "Combined Type". The question resolves on the week ending 2026-10-24, as posted 2026-10-30. [dataset](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
- 2026-09-26: this is the latest week that would have been available by the cutoff. National HCOV percent positive was **0.68%**, from 19,649 tests. [dataset](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json?$where=level='National'%20AND%20pathogen='HCOV')
- Recent national weekly values for 2026 (testing volume is rising, which is normal in autumn):
  - 08-01: 0.44
  - 08-08: 0.66
  - 08-15: 0.50
  - 08-22: 0.59
  - 08-29: 0.67
  - 09-05: 0.63
  - 09-12: 0.54
  - 09-19: 0.65
  - 09-26: 0.68

  [dataset](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
- Earlier in 2026: the spring season was declining in May (1.99% on 05-02) and reached a summer floor of about 0.44 to 0.62% in late June to early August. [dataset](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The target week ends 2026-10-24, and its data are not posted until about 2026-10-30.
- Summer and early autumn 2026 levels (about 0.55 to 0.68%) are roughly twice the same weeks in 2025 (about 0.27 to 0.36%). They are below 2024 (0.75 to 0.92%) and similar to 2023 (0.41 to 0.57%).

## 3. Recent news
- I found no news coverage of seasonal (non-SARS-CoV-2) coronaviruses for autumn 2026. CDC's routine NREVSS updates appear to be the only relevant signal. I did not find any reporting disruption or methods change announced before 2026-10-05.

## 4. Base rates (national HCOV Combined, from the same dataset)
Late-September value compared with the late-October week about 4 weeks later:

| Season | Late-Sept value | Late-Oct value | Change | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2020 | 09-26: 0.16 | 10-24: 0.21 | +0.05 | ×1.3 |
| 2021 | 09-25: 0.73 | 10-23: 0.58 | -0.15 | ×0.79 |
| 2022 | 09-24: 0.28 | 10-22: 0.42 | +0.14 | ×1.5 |
| 2023 | 09-23: 0.52 | 10-21: 0.44 | -0.08 | ×0.85 |
| 2024 | 09-28: 0.75 | 10-26: 1.53 | +0.78 | ×2.0 |
| 2025 | 09-27: 0.27 | 10-25: 0.33 | +0.06 | ×1.2 |

- Late-October values in past years:
  - 2021: 0.58
  - 2022: 0.42
  - 2023: 0.44 (10-21), then 0.66 (10-28)
  - 2024: 1.14 (10-19), then 1.53 (10-26)
  - 2025: 0.30 (10-18), then 0.33 (10-25)
- Pattern: October is usually the trough, or the very start of the winter rise. In most years the 4-week ratio is between 0.8 and 1.5. 2024 was the outlier: an early, strong season that doubled the value in 4 weeks.
- Week-to-week noise at these levels is about ±0.1 percentage point. Examples: 2025-08-16 to 08-23 went 0.31 to 0.56 to 0.35, and 2026-08-01 to 08-08 went 0.44 to 0.66.
- 2026 is running higher than 2025. If you apply the historical ratios to 0.68, you get a range of about 0.55 to 1.0, and up to about 1.4 in a 2024-type early season.
- Revisions: values are reposted every week. Recent weeks can shift by a few hundredths as late reports come in.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or expert forecasts for NREVSS seasonal coronavirus positivity.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- CDC posts NREVSS updates weekly, around Thursday or Friday. The updates on about 10-09, 10-16 and 10-23 will show the weeks ending 10-03, 10-10 and 10-17. The resolving post is expected about 2026-10-30.
- The usual seasonal start of the winter coronavirus rise falls in late October to November. Rising test volumes, which are normal in autumn, can push positivity in either direction.
- Watch for possible federal reporting disruptions, such as a government shutdown or a change to CDC data operations. I found no specific reports of one before the cutoff.

Sources:
- [CDC data.cdc.gov rgnm-fkqb (NREVSS percent positivity)](https://data.cdc.gov/resource/rgnm-fkqb.json)
